en: The Questions of Milinda,
Great Chapter 11:
The Question on Faith Characterized by Leaping Forward (Sampakkhandana-lakkhaṇa-saddhā-pañha)
“Venerable sir, in what way does faith have the characteristic of leaping forward?

“Just as, great king, when a practitioner of yoga sees the minds of others liberated, he leaps forward toward the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or arahantship;
he exerts himself in yoga for the sake of attaining what has not been attained, for the sake of realizing what has not been realized.”
“For the attainment of what has not yet been attained, for the realization of what has not yet been realized.
“In this way, Great King, faith has the characteristic of leaping forward,” [he said].
“Give me a simile,” [the king requested].
“Just as, great king, if a great cloud were to rain upon a mountain above, that water, flowing down according to its slope,
would fill the mountain clefts, ravines, and gullies, and thereby fill the river; and that river, overflowing both its banks, would flow on,
and then a great multitude of people might come and [perceive] the shallowness or the depth of that river.”
Or, being ignorant and terrified, one might stand on the bank, paralyzed with fear;

then another person, having arrived and considering his own strength and power, would bind his loincloth tightly, leap in, and cross over; seeing that person crossed, the great multitude of people would also cross.
In the same way, Great King, when a practitioner of yoga sees the minds of others liberated, he leaps forward toward the fruit of stream-entry,
the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or arahantship; he applies himself to yoga for the attainment of what has not been attained,
for the realization of what has not been realized, and for the direct experience of what has not been directly experienced.
"Thus, Great King, faith has the characteristic of leaping forward.
This was also spoken, Great King, by the Blessed One in the excellent Saṃyutta Nikāya:
'By means of faith one crosses the flood...'"
“By heedfulness one crosses the ocean;
by energy one overcomes suffering;
by wisdom one is purified.”
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena!
Thus ends the eleventh chapter, the Question on Faith characterized by Leaping Forward.
